author: val
body: Pins widget text inside its box. Third and last of the three overflow defects in this renderer, after the gauge fill and the caret that codex/test/gop-render-clamp holds. This one took an argument the primitives did not have: neither gr-emit-text nor gop-buf-put-text-role carries a width or a right edge, so the box was information they were never given.

author: val
body: Sixty characters at nine pixels each is 540, past the right edge of a widget pinned to 200 and past the 400-pixel buffer as well. The buffer clips at its own edge in both worlds, which is why the scan stops short of it: the question is where the WIDGET ends, not where the buffer does.

author: val
body: The label is measured rather than the input because an input also draws a caret in the same colour and the two could not then be told apart. The sibling is a gauge rather than a label because a label emits text and no box: a gauge at value 0 draws no fill at all, and its background and border are not the pal-fg this scans for.

author: val
body: The unbounded row is not decoration and must not be dropped. It draws the same string at the same origin through the FREE-STANDING entry point, which still runs to the buffer width, and requires it to still be there. A fix applied to the shared primitive instead of the widget path would turn outside green and this row red, and that is a different behaviour from the one intended. inside is the control: the first characters sit at the content origin in every version, so neither defect nor fix can move it.

author: val
body: Both sabotages fired on exactly their own row, against seed 6867EA9D. Dropping the widget bound at gop-render-label moved outside 0 to 1 and left inside and unbounded at 1. Bounding the free-standing path as well, by passing gb.gb-width / 2 from gop-buf-put-text-role, moved unbounded 1 to 0 and left the other two. The control held at 1 in both.
